motivation: results_v2.md section 14.4: DualGuard and PortGuard conflict under sustained pressure

rule.data: validation seeds 2000-2002, dedicated ports, D1-D3, A1-A7 + gap sweep + benign-only
rule.feasible: mean benign harm on A1-A7 <= v2.1's + 0.5 points and benign-only harm <= v2.1's + 0.1 points
rule.objective: minimise mean benign harm over the gap sweep
rule.tie_break: within 0.05 points: lower mean attacker occupancy over the gap sweep, then fewer overflow seconds
rule.fallback: if none is feasible: minimise total constraint violation (points), then the objective
rule.applies_to: the selected candidate is v2.1+pfs4b; pfs-sel is PortGuard alone with the selected share and q

hypotheses.H1: dedicated, gaps <= 1 s: v2.1+pfs4b harms fewer benign flows than the step-4 composition v2.1+pfs
hypotheses.H2: dedicated, A1-A7: v2.1+pfs4b is non-inferior to v2.1 (mean harm difference <= 0.5 points)
hypotheses.H3: dedicated: v2.1+pfs4b mean harm <= 3 % at every refresh gap
hypotheses.H4: dedicated, A1-A7: v2.1+pfs4b harms fewer than PortGuard alone with the same share and q (pfs-sel)
hypotheses.H5: shared, gaps <= 1 s: v2.1+pfs4b harms fewer than v2.1
hypotheses.H6: distributed, A1-A7: v2.1+pfs4b is non-inferior to v2.1 (<= 0.5 points)
hypotheses.H7: distributed, gaps <= 1 s (expected negative): v2.1+pfs4b does not reduce harm vs v2.1

development_note: modes and weighted shares were developed on training seed 1000 only
statistics: cluster bootstrap and cluster Wilcoxon over (domain, seed), Holm across H1-H7 tests
